fixes.explanation: Protect! "Like birds hovering overhead, so the LORD of Hosts will protect Jerusalem." (Isaiah 31:5). Birds hover over what they're watching over, and that's the picture here. The verse goes on: "He will shield it and deliver it; He will pass over it and preserve it." Good, warm words after all that woe.

Horses, baker! Isaiah says they "…rely on horses…" and then he keeps going with "…their abundance of chariots…" and "…their multitude of horsemen." (Isaiah 31:1). That's a whole stable and a parking lot of chariots. Everything they're leaning on has hooves or wheels, and none of it is the LORD.

I see why you'd think it, but it's the opposite. Isaiah says of them, "They do not look to the Holy One of Israel; they do not seek the LORD." (Isaiah 31:1). Their trust is in the horses, the chariots and the horsemen. They don't look to Him.

Yes! Isaiah says of the LORD, "He does not call back His words." (Isaiah 31:2). Once He's spoken, it stands. No take-backs. I wish I had that kind of follow-through. I once said "just one more cookie" about forty times.
Close, but no. Isaiah doesn't say anything about hiding. He says, "He does not call back His words." (Isaiah 31:2). They aren't getting pulled back.

Other way around. The lion "…is not terrified by their shouting or subdued by their clamor…" (Isaiah 31:4). The shepherds are called out against it, and there's shouting and clamor. It still isn't terrified or subdued.

Not gifts. The message says, "Return to the One against whom you have so blatantly rebelled, O children of Israel." (Isaiah 31:6). It's the coming back that matters here. Nobody's asked to show up with a wrapped present.

Idols! The message says, "…every one of you will reject the idols of silver and gold that your own hands have sinfully made." (Isaiah 31:7). Their own hands made them, and the verse calls that sinful. I stamp cookies, but I have never once asked a cookie for advice.

Silver and gold do sound like crown material. But the verse says, "…every one of you will reject the idols of silver and gold that your own hands have sinfully made." (Isaiah 31:7). They're idols, not crowns, and their own hands made them. On that day, every one of them will reject them.
Right! The LORD says, "a sword will devour them, but not one made by mortals." (Isaiah 31:8). Assyria falls "…not by the sword of man…" No blacksmith signed that blade.
Egypt came up earlier in the passage, but it isn't named in this verse. The LORD says, "a sword will devour them, but not one made by mortals." (Isaiah 31:8). So the sword is not one made by mortals.

Good thinking, but that's not what the LORD says. Assyria will fall "…not by the sword of man; a sword will devour them, but not one made by mortals." (Isaiah 31:8). The sword He describes is not one made by mortals.
False, baker. The LORD says, "They will flee before the sword, and their young men will be put to forced labor." (Isaiah 31:8). Nobody stands and fights. That's the opposite of standing their ground.

Yes! "…their princes will panic at the sight of the battle standard…" declares the LORD (Isaiah 31:9). The sight of the standard is what sets them off. I'd panic too if the oven timer went off and I hadn't started the dough.
